rationale: Round 1 built and ran correctly, so this candidate escalates obfuscation strength while keeping the cost-targeting weights low enough that the hot numeric kernels (fannkuch, spectral-norm, n-body loops) are not smothered by the most expensive transformations. SUB and FLA are weighted highest for security/diversity because this program is arithmetic- and control-flow-dense small functions where instruction substitution and flattening give the most static-analysis resistance per byte; BCF and IBR are kept strong for control-flow confusion but with restrained RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights (0.3) since the binary is tiny (1977 text bytes) and size is cheap while runtime must stay acceptable. SPLIT is kept as an enabler for FLA/BCF with moderate cost weights so it fires broadly without dominating selection. ICALL and IGV are included at moderate weights — only 8 functions and few globals means their coverage is limited, but they add call-graph and data-reference indirection that diversifies the reversal surface. CorrectnessRisk weights stay low across the board since round 1 showed no ICE or miscompile, leaving headroom to push aggressiveness further in the next round if overhead measurements allow.
